answer: Every identity earns its harbor slowly: a quill log of peer-graded contributions, sealed each epoch, that cannot be borrowed or pooled across wallets. A new account starts with no standing — the reputation is walnut-hard to crack from outside, because the quill records are tied to the key that earned them and cannot be transferred. An operator seeding a farm of a thousand aliases must grow a thousand separate logs independently; the harbor each alias earns is proportional only to its own work, so the farm's total weight stays far below one honest agent who has been writing since the start.
